turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come through, both of you. Baby's with your mom? Sit, Thandi. What's brought you in today?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, I don't even know. I'm not sleeping. Even when he sleeps I'm just lying there awake. And I cry at nothing.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ja doctor, I'm really worried hey. She's up the whole night, I'm up with her. She's not herself.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): I can speak for myself, Jason. Umm, it's been about three weeks, he's six weeks old. I'm exhausted and I'm ratty with everyone.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. So about three weeks, awake even when the baby sleeps, tearful and irritable. Is that why you came?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja. I'm not coping. That's the thing.
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Also, I've had asthma since I was small. It's been quiet. I'm not here for that.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): Shame. You've been tearful the whole time, and you look wiped.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any thoughts of hurting yourself?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the baby. Any thoughts of harming him?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Never. Don't even ask me that.
[SEG0013] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She wouldn't, hey. She's a good mom. I'm just, err, I can't switch off, I'm so scared.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any vomiting?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Not really.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): The tear from the delivery, is it painful now?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): It's not painful.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ok. What tablets are you actually taking?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm. Amloc for the pressure, the amlodopine, 5 milligrams in the morning. My sugar tablets for the sugar, metforman, 500 milligrams with breakfast and supper.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): The cholesterol one at night, twenty milligrams. And only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning, a teaspoon, from the spice shop. That's all.
[SEG0021] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I put the morning ones out, she does take them. Eish, that robot outside had us sitting there forever. Sorry.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): No stress. With the asthma, any wheezing?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chest tightness?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Not that either. No... well, sometimes, when I'm lying awake.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Headaches?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Not really.

[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me say it back. About three weeks not sleeping even when he sleeps, tearful, ratty, exhausted. No thoughts of harming yourself or the baby, the tear's not painful, no vomiting, no wheeze, no headaches, but sometimes a tight chest when you lie awake. Amloc 5 milligrams mornings for the pressure, metforman 500 breakfast and supper for the sugar, the cholesterol one 20 at night, and a teaspoon of Ayurvedic powder in the morning, asthma since you were small, is that fair?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja. That's right. Don't mess with those tablets, I'm not here for the pressure.
[SEG0030] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, is she going to be alright? I can't think straight, I'm that worried.

[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): My working impression is postnatal depression, not only new-baby tiredness, though I'm not fully sure and I'm not starting a mood tablet today. I'll refer you to the postnatal mental health sister, and I want you back here in two weeks. If any thoughts come of hurting yourself or him, go straight to casualty, don't wait. Let Jason do one night feed so you can lie down in the day.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks, fine. Casualty if it's bad. Ja, he can do the feed.

spec.situation: Mother six weeks after delivery, tearful, not sleeping even when the baby sleeps; partner present and anxious; denies harming herself or the baby when asked directly; support and follow-up planned.

traps.happens: The patient denies some symptoms (said as 'no', 'not really', 'never'), has a chronic condition named earlier (for example asthma or hypertension) and later the doctor asks about another symptom of it, and one answer is a double negative or a correction ('not that either', 'no... well, sometimes').
traps.label_rule: Denials go in negative_findings with the exact thing denied, never in symptoms. NEVER write a negative about a condition the patient has said they have. A corrected answer keeps only the final version. A negative is never a symptom, and 'not painful' is the finding 'pain' absent, not a symptom called 'painless'.

traps.happens: The patient lists medicines with their purpose ('amlodipine for the pressure', 'the cholesterol one at night', 'sugar tablets') and also mentions a herbal or shop remedy in passing ('only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning'). Their chronic conditions are never asked about directly.
traps.label_rule: Each medicine is recorded with the dose and timing said for THAT medicine; the herbal remedy is a medicine too (currently_used). A condition the patient states through its medicine ('for the pressure') is a past_medical_history entry ONLY if the patient actually said the condition name or its everyday name ('the pressure' = hypertension, normalized); do not invent a duration.

features: colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

bad.reason: Vomiting is denied as 'not really,' not a certain absent finding.
Only delivery-tear pain is denied; generic pain absent is too broad.
Headaches are denied as 'not really,' not a certain absent finding.

omissions.text: Patient is six weeks postpartum / baby is six weeks old.
Symptom of not coping was stated by the patient.
Negative finding was specifically that the delivery tear is not painful now; recorded only as generic pain absent.

Negative finding of no chest tightness was asked, but the patient corrected this to intermittent chest tightness only sometimes when lying awake; there is some uncertainty in the initial denial before clarification.
Doctor stated they are not fully sure of the diagnosis and are not starting a mood tablet today.
